newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan says Israel pushes peace process to crisis.
newsitem.headline: Jordan says Israel pushes peace process to crisis.

text.p: Jordan warned Israel on Tuesday it was pushing the Middle East into crisis by dictating terms of its withdrawal from West Bank areas and building Jewish homes in Arab East Jerusalem.

Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti said Arab-Israeli peace had reached "a very real crisis" because of Israeli plans to build 6,500 Jewish houses in East Jerusalem and its unilateral decision to pull back from just nine percent of West Bank land.
"Jordan rejects these decision," Kabariti said after meeting Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai. "The Israelis...have to resort to the negotiating table, not to dictate the facts."
Kabariti said King Hussein had sent two letters to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stating Jordan's "clear position" on the settlements and the West Bank withdrawal.

He gave no details but the Jordanian monarch, who signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994, was quoted by Israel's Maariv newspaper as writing: "You are destroying the peace and I haven't an ounce of trust in you."
The Israeli leader, visiting Moscow, was quoted by Israel army radio as retorting that King Hussein's comments were unbalanced.
But the king, who last year urged dismayed Arab leaders to give Netanyahu a chance after ousting Nobel Peace Laureate Shimon Peres, said he could not stay silent.
"I have a duty towards the Israeli public as well as towards the Jordanians and Palestinians," he told Israeli journalists.
Mordechai said he did not discuss the king's message to Netanyahu during his talks with the Jordanian monarch.
"I am sure they will find a way to negotiate. There are some misunderstandings but I am sure we can overcome those problems," he said. "Both of them are honest and respect each other."

While King Hussein hosted a lunch for Mordechai, Islamist and independent members of parliament called for an abrogation of Jordan's 1994 peace treaty with Israel and criticised the government's ties with the Jewish state.
"What pressure does Israel feel when Israeli officials repeatedly come to Amman and find a welcoming and warm atmosphere," former prime minister Taher al-Masri asked.
Many of Jordan's 4.2 million people are Palestinians with strong famly ties across the Jordan River and officials fear domestic repercussions if violence erupts in Palestinian areas.

Kabariti said King Hussein will stress Jordan's opposition to the Israeli moves when he goes to the United States on Friday for talks with President Bill Clinton. The king's visit follows trips by Netanyahu, Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
Kabariti warned Israel that Palestinian authorities could not be accountable for any outburst of anger when construction starts on the Jewish homes in Jabal Abu Ghoneim, called Har Homa by Israel.

"They cannot expect the Palestinians to work as policemen for their bulldozers when they move into Abu Ghoneim," Kabariti said. Sixty-one Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers were killed in clashes last September after Netanyahu opened a new entrance to an archaeology tunnel near Moslem holy sites in East Jerusalem.
